'''Isador Lubin''' (9 June 1896 – 6 July 1978) was the head of the [[U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics]] from 1933 to 1946, and president of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 1946.

== Career ==
[[File:1,500,000 drop in employment, Senate Committee told by government labor statistics chief. Washington, D.C., Jan. 4. Armed with many charts and his head full of figures, Isador Lubin, Chief LCCN2016872803.jpg|thumb|Isador Lubin in 1937]]
During the [[First World War]], at the [[United States Food Administration|U.S. Food Administration]], Lubin analyzed labor and price policy related to food production for the Allied Nations. Later at the [[War Industries Board]]’s Price Section, he studied the effect of price shifts on the output of the petroleum and rubber industries.<ref name=WasserDolfman/><ref name=commish/>

He was as an instructor at the Institute of Economics and earned a Ph.D. there in 1926. It became part of the [[Brookings Institution]] in 1927.  Lubin's book ''Miners' Wages and the Cost of Coal'' was accepted as a dissertation.<ref name=WasserDolfman/>

"In 1932, as adviser to Senator [[Robert M. La Follette Jr.]], he pioneered the notion of government responsibility for the [[national accounts]]."<ref name=WasserDolfman/>

Lubin was appointed head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) by [[Frances Perkins]] in July 1933 and stayed in the position until January 1946.<ref name=commish>[http://www.bls.gov/bls/history/commissioners/lubin.htm BLS history, Commissioners Isador Lubin] at bls.gov</ref><ref>{{Cite book
|last=Blumberg|first=Barbara|publisher=Oxford University Press|title=American National Biography|chapter=Isador Lubin|access-date=2013-12-08|year=1999|chapter-url=http://h-net.msu.edu/cgi-bin/logbrowse.pl?trx=vx&list=h-demog&month=9911&msg=v6UwLvrXKd8mH9XxEiowVw }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=McKinzie|first=Richard D|title=Dr. Isador Lubin Oral History Interview|work=Truman Library|access-date=2013-12-08|date=1974-06-26|url=http://www.trumanlibrary.org/oralhist/lubini.htm }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Remembering Isador Lubin, 1896-1978: some tributes and recollections gathered for his friends|year=1980|access-date=2013-12-08|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8Qt6AAAAIAAJ }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Edward R. Stettinius, Jr., Chairman of U.S. Steel. Isador Lubin, left, Commissioner of Labor Statistics. Leon Henderson, right, new S.E.C. Commissioner|work=Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Catalog|access-date=2013-12-08|url=https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/hec2009013405/ }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Map depicts significant story on pickup in American industry. Washington, D.C. March 30. Tow lines on this chart hanging in the office of Isador Lubin, Commissioner of Labor Statistics, U.S. Department of Labor, tell a significant story of the pickup ...|work=Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Catalog|access-date=2013-12-08|url=https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/hec2009009166/ }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Economic trends: testimony of Isador Lubin, United States Commissioner of Labor Statistics, before the Temporary National Economic Committee|work=U.S. Government Printing Office|access-date=2013-12-08|year=1939|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6OhZAAAAYAAJ |last1=Lubin|first1=Isador}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine|title=National Affairs: New Adviser|magazine=TIME|access-date=2013-12-08|date=1941-05-26|url=http://content.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,765611,00.html }}</ref> For much of this time, Lubin had an office in the White House's [[West Wing]] "and served as special statistical adviser to President [[Franklin Roosevelt]]."<ref name=WasserDolfman/> Lubin was sometimes described as a member of President Roosevelt's "[[Brain Trust|brain trust]]."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Hess|first=John L|title=ISADOR LUBIN DIES, 82 - IN 'BRAIN TRUST' - Economist for Roosevelt Served on United Nations Missions|work=New York Times|access-date=2013-12-08|date=1978-07-08|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1978/07/08/archives/isador-lubin-dies-82-in-brain-trust-economist-for-roosevelt-served.html }}</ref> In 1944 he was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm View/Search Fellows of the ASA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |date=2016-06-16 }}, accessed 2016-07-23.</ref>

In 1941 Lubin authorized BLS to start a research group at [[Harvard University]] directed by [[Wassily Leontief]] which constructed the first official [[input-output model|table of U.S. industry inputs and outputs]]." In 1945, Roosevelt appointed Lubin as Minister to the Allied Reparations Commission.<ref name=WasserDolfman/>

"In his presidential address to the American Statistical Society in January [1947], Lubin emphasized [the role] of statistics in modern economic society and the value to the free world of pertinent data."<ref name=WasserDolfman>{{Cite journal|last=Wasser|first=Solidelle F|author2=Michael L Dolfman|title=BLS and the Marshall Plan: The Forgotten Story|journal=Monthly Labor Review|access-date=2013-12-08|date=2005-06-01|url=http://www.bls.gov/opub/mlr/2005/06/art4full.pdf }}</ref>

Lubin was appointed the Industrial Commissioner of [[New York state]] from 1955 to 1958 by Governor [[W. Averell Harriman]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Papers of Isador Lubin|work=Franklin D. Roosevelt Library & Museum|access-date=2013-12-08|url=http://docs.fdrlibrary.marist.edu:8000/findbrow.cgi?collection=Lubin,+Isador }}</ref>

== Personal and legacy ==
In 1952 Lubin married the former Carol Riegelman (1909–2005), a longtime consultant to the UN/[[ILO]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Commemorative Chairs: Isador and Carol Lubin |work=Franklin and Eleanor Roosevelt Institute |access-date=2013-12-08 |url=http://newdeal.feri.org/kiosk/profile.cfm?QID=2873 }}</ref> He had two daughters by a previous marriage to Ann Shumaker Lubin, the editor of "Progressive Education" and co-author of the book, "The Child-Centered School" (1928):<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.channelingreality.com/TTT/Biographies/isador_lubin_biography.htm|title=Isador Lubin Biography & Articles|access-date=July 15, 2019}}</ref> Alice Lubin Everitt and [https://bulletin.swarthmore.edu/bulletin-issue-archive/archive_p=277.html Ann Lubin Buttenwieser].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carol Riegelman Lubin Papers, 1909-2005: A Finding Aid |work=Arthur and Elizabeth Schlesinger Library on the History of Women in America, Harvard University Library |access-date=2013-12-08 |url=http://oasis.lib.harvard.edu/oasis/deliver/~sch01396 }}</ref>

Fellowships named for Dr. Lubin were established at [[Brandeis University]] and [[The New School]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr. Isidor Lubin Honored on 70th Birthday; Lauded for His Activities|work=Jewish Telegraphic Agency|access-date=2013-12-08|url=https://www.jta.org/1966/06/10/archive/dr-isidor-lubin-honored-on-70th-birthday-lauded-for-his-activities }}</ref><ref>[http://www.brandeis.edu/global/admissions/tuition/ Tuition and Financial Aid] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131216083543/http://www.brandeis.edu/global/admissions/tuition/ |date=2013-12-16 }} at Brandeis International Business School</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Scholarships and Awards: Isador Lubin Fellowship|work=The New School for Public Engagement|access-date=2013-12-08|url=http://www.newschool.edu/public-engagement/milano-school-scholarships-awards/ }}</ref>
